title: Employer proof of wage payment strengthens a remedy route without proving worker receipt, adequacy, or durable payroll correction
source_unit: U.S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division PAID program and performance release
geography: United States; DOL Wage and Hour Division PAID program

observations.period: Current PAID program architecture checked September 19, 2026

denominator.unit: employers and affected employees considered for PAID; no public episode or worker-level follow-up denominator

trigger.value: employer self-audit identifies potential minimum-wage, overtime, or qualifying FMLA violations

review_and_payment_rule.value: WHD reviews calculations; employer pays within 15 days of the summary and provides proof of payment and practice correction

employee_choice.value: employee may accept or decline the offered payment

worker_receipt_and_durability.unit: missing named worker delivery, cashing, adequacy, remaining loss, household effect, later payroll, recurrence, trust, and exit

mechanism.value: A program can insert employer proof and prospective practice correction between remedy calculation and worker-level recovery, strengthening institutional accountability without closing the lived outcome

observations.method: Structured extraction from official DOL PAID program and questions-and-answers pages; program requirements are retained separately from named employer compliance and worker-confirmed recovery.
observations.uncertainty: The public architecture does not identify an employer episode, affected workers, payment instruments, worker receipt/cashing, adequacy, remaining loss, household effect, later work, trust, recurrence, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Employers and employees considered for voluntary PAID correction; no public worker-level or employer-level outcome sample is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Proof supplied to WHD can coexist with non-cashing, insufficient compensation, unresolved household loss, continued dependence, or a worker declining payment for an unknown reason.

observations.period: PAID performance release covering actions concluded through September 15, 2019

back_wages.unit: more than U.S. dollars reported put into employees' hands

aggregate_delivery.value: reported wages put into employees' hands through PAID

employee_level_recovery.unit: missing employee identity, amount, payment date, cashing, adequacy, residual loss, household effect, later payroll, and exit

mechanism.value: Aggregate reported delivery can demonstrate program reach while leaving the distribution and durability of recovery unresolved

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official DOL WHD PAID performance release; aggregate employees and back wages are retained separately from recipient-level delivery and durability.
observations.uncertainty: The release provides no employee-level identifiers, amounts, payment rails, delivery or cashing record, adequacy, remaining loss, household outcome, later payroll, trust, recurrence, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Employees in PAID actions concluded by the reported period; no worker, employer, industry, or wage-loss subgroup outcome is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: More than $4 million put into employees' hands is stronger than a program rule, but it is not an independently verified worker recovery rate or proof of durable compliance.

boundary: This record establishes a public wage-remedy architecture and aggregate PAID delivery result. It does not establish individual worker receipt, adequacy, account correction, durable payroll compliance, household recovery, trust, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from official DOL PAID pages and performance release; employer self-audits, payroll, worker identities, payments, and restricted files are not retained.
